subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Robert Fortune: The Tea Thief
description: A short lesson to help you apply Robert Fortune: The Tea Thief.

hook.text: In 1848, Scottish botanist Robert Fortune disguised himself as a Chinese merchant and stole China's tea secrets for Britain.

buildup.text: The British East India Company hired Fortune to smuggle tea plants and manufacturing knowledge out of China's interior.

discovery.text: Fortune learned that black and green tea come from the same plant—a secret China had kept for centuries. Processing, not variety.

twist.text: He shipped 20,000 tea plants and expert Chinese tea makers to India. Britain built its tea empires on this theft.

climax.text: Fortune's espionage ended China's tea monopoly and shifted global power. India surpassed China as the world's top tea exporter.

punchline.text: Disguise, deception, 20,000 plants. The biggest heist in beverage history.

quiz.question: What crucial tea secret did Robert Fortune discover in China?
options: Black and green tea come from the same plant—processing makes the difference

details.summary: Scottish botanist Robert Fortune disguised himself as a Chinese merchant in 1848 and smuggled tea plants, seeds, and manufacturing secrets out of China on behalf of the British East India Company. His theft broke China's tea monopoly and established India as a rival tea-producing powerhouse.
details.whyItMatters: Fortune's espionage is one of history's biggest acts of industrial theft. It shifted the global tea industry from Chinese dominance to British-controlled Indian production.
takeaways: Fortune disguised himself to infiltrate Chinese tea-growing regions
He smuggled plants, seeds, and processing knowledge to India
His actions broke China's monopoly and built Indian tea production

faq.question: How did Robert Fortune successfully smuggle tea out of China?
faq.answer: Fortune shaved his head, wore Chinese clothing, and traveled with a local guide to remote tea regions. He collected plants and seeds while learning processing techniques, then shipped everything to British India for cultivation.

faq.question: What impact did Fortune's theft have on the global tea industry?
faq.answer: Within decades, British India and Ceylon became the world's largest tea exporters, devastating China's tea trade. The shift created the large-scale plantation model that still dominates global tea production today.
